note: The change ledger. These are facts about the work rather than samples, so they are committed as data and rendered into a table by analysis/reporting.mjs. 'effect' must be either a measured number with its source table, or the literal string 'not measured' - never an estimate dressed as a result.

changes.change: Recovered a per-stage profile from container logs
changes.what: The pipeline's timing decorators printed to stdout and nothing persisted them. The platform retains container stdout, so the profile was pulled back over its API from real production runs with no instrumentation change.
changes.detail: Ten stages, n=5, reconciling to the independently printed job total within 0.03 s

changes.change: Fixed the timing decorator so repeated stages accumulate
changes.what: The decorator overwrote a stage's time on each call, so any job invoking a stage more than once reported only the last invocation. Every multi-segment word-replacement job was affected.
changes.detail: Every timing table on this site flows through the fixed code path

changes.change: Pinned the dependency graph and made the image buildable
changes.what: 28 of 62 requirement lines carried no version, so every rebuild resolved a different environment and nothing had rebuilt cleanly in roughly sixteen months.
changes.detail: 221 packages pinned; first green build of the repository since May 2025

changes.change: Found and fixed a mixed-CUDA torch stack
changes.what: A version pin does not identify a build variant. Pinning torch to a version installed a CUDA 12.4 wheel from the public index, while the build's own later step installed CUDA 12.1 builds of torchaudio and torchvision. torchaudio then refuses to import, and the pipeline imports it before serving its first request.
changes.detail: The container reached a running state; a full clip completed in 398 s

changes.change: Made the sampler seedable per run
changes.what: The audio-to-expression model seeded once at construction, so the first prediction in a warm process was reproducible and every later one was not. Two runs of one clip shared zero identical frames out of 1074.
changes.detail: Prerequisite for a paired A/B, and for the cache in the same section

changes.what: Roadmap item, premised on the GPU being under-fed at batch 4. Exposed as one environment variable so a single build serves both sides of the comparison.
changes.detail: -0.14% once the session drift measured by a repeated baseline is removed, and inside the output noise floor: rejected. The renderer waits on video decode, not on arithmetic

changes.change: fp16 autocast in the neural renderer
changes.what: Roadmap item. Also exposed as one environment variable, default off.
changes.detail: -0.41% drift-adjusted and inside the output noise floor: rejected as null. Its output sits no further from the baseline than a repeat of the baseline itself, so this is not a fidelity finding

changes.change: Asynchronous host-to-device transfers in the renderer
changes.what: Roadmap item, partially implemented: non_blocking on six host-to-device copies. Pinned memory already existed; CUDA streams were not built.
changes.detail: Always on, so it is inside every arm including the baseline and cannot be isolated by this design

changes.change: cuDNN autotuning scoped to the render loop
changes.what: Not a roadmap item. The animator's seeding helper disables cuDNN autotuning process-wide as a side effect, and the renderer inherits it: hundreds of convolutions at one fixed input shape, run without autotuned kernels.
changes.detail: +0.50% drift-adjusted: rejected. The raw +1.89% was almost entirely session drift, which a repeated baseline caught

changes.change: Paste-back composites only the mask bounding box
changes.what: Where the warped mask is zero the composite writes the source back over itself. Restricting it to the mask's bounding box is bit-exact by construction rather than an approximation.
changes.detail: Bit-identical across 44 cases and 400 random transforms; 1.55x to 2.90x on the function, which is about 14% of the timed stage

changes.change: Output sanity checks on every generated video
changes.what: A timing harness cannot see a black frame, a frozen output, or a face whose mouth never moves. An arm that is faster because it produced garbage would otherwise read as a win.
changes.detail: 16 of 16 open-dataset outputs pass, confirmed by automated checks and by frame inspection

changes.what: The quality harness loaded its whole result file at start, held it for minutes, then wrote it back whole. Two concurrent scorings destroyed one another's results.
changes.detail: A completed three-clip result set was lost this way before the fix; writes now merge and rename atomically

changes.change: A baseline repeated as the last pass of the session
changes.what: Produces no information about any optimization. Its only job is to measure how much the machine itself moved between the first arm and the last.
changes.detail: +1.85% slower than the identical first pass, on the same three clips with the same seed and no code change. This is the drift correction applied to every arm above, and it is why none of them was kept

changes.change: The whole branch measured against the unmodified upstream code
changes.what: Checks the reverse risk: that the accumulated changes cost something incidental even where each was individually null.
changes.detail: -0.47% against the adjacent baseline with mixed per-clip signs, and every output inside the noise floor: the branch is performance-neutral

changes.change: Deterministic kernels behind a second flag
changes.what: Asks torch for deterministic algorithms and a fixed cuBLAS workspace on top of the reseed, to test whether the pipeline can reproduce its own output exactly.
changes.detail: 0 of 751 frames identical across two runs at one seed, and a 10.6% to 13.3% wall clock cost: the floor does not move, so the flag stays off. The nondeterminism sits outside torch, which is what decides the cache design

changes.change: A third baseline, with the accumulated output cleared first
changes.what: Tests whether the session drift has an avoidable cause. The pipeline writes eighteen intermediate videos per job into one directory, which had reached 20 GB. Free space was ruled out first: the volume stayed 39 % full.
changes.detail: Recovered 0.91 of the 1.85 points of drift, consistent in sign across all three clips. Smaller than the 2.28 % repeat spread, so it is treated as grounds for clearing the directory between arms, not as a result
